lessons.title: Places in town
lessons.scenario: You and Smarty stand on a balcony and look over the town. Name the places you can see.

items.note: Say 'park' for a green place with trees and grass where people walk and play.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat sits on the grass under a big tree in a sunny park, with a bench and a small pond behind him.

items.note: Say 'school' for the place where children go to learn with their teacher.

image.describe: A friendly school building with a flag, big windows and a playground; Smarty the black cat and Mia walk to the gate with school bags.

items.note: Say 'hospital' for the big building where doctors help people who are ill.

image.describe: A big hospital building with a red cross icon above the door (a cross only, no words); Smarty the black cat waves outside with Ben.

items.note: Say 'bank' for the place where people keep their money safe.

image.describe: A solid bank building with tall columns and a round gold coin icon on the front (no words); Smarty the black cat looks at it with Sam.

items.note: Say 'café' for a small place where you drink tea or coffee and eat cake.

image.describe: A cosy small café with a striped awning and little tables outside; Smarty the black cat, Mia and Sam sit with cups and a cake.

practice.prompt: Which word is a green place with trees and grass?
practice.explanation: A park has trees and grass. A bank is for money and a school is for learning.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for the place word after The.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: This is + the + a place says what a building is.

practice.prompt: You keep your money safe here. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: You keep money in the bank, not in a hospital or school.

practice.prompt: You want tea and cake. Where do you go?
practice.explanation: A café is a small place for tea and cake.

practice.prompt: Say the phrase aloud. You can retry if recognition mishears you.
practice.explanation: You described a place in town. You can also say The park is small.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for bank. The word before is is the place.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: Is links the place with a describing word.

practice.prompt: Which place is for doctors and ill people?
practice.explanation: A hospital is where doctors help people.

story.hook: Smarty looks at the town from the balcony. Which place is new?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Look, Smarty! I like the park.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: The café is small, but the cake is delicious.

questions.explanation: Mia says she likes the park.
Sam says the café is small.
Mia says the hospital is new.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat, Mia and Sam stand on a sunny balcony and look over a small town with a park, a café, a school and a hospital below.

mission.setup: You and Smarty look over the town from the balcony. Say which place you like.

turns.smarty: I like the park. And you?
turns.hint: Say I like the + a place word.

turns.smarty: The café is small. Is the park big?
turns.hint: Answer Yes or No. You can say it is big or it is small.

lessons.title: More places
lessons.scenario: Ben, Ana and Smarty look at more places from the balcony. Say which ones you like.

items.example: I buy bread at the supermarket.
items.note: Say 'supermarket' for a big shop where you can buy food and many things.

image.describe: A large supermarket with a shopping cart outside and baskets of fruit and bread by the door; Smarty pushes the cart with Ana.

items.example: I read a book in the library.
items.note: Say 'library' for the quiet place with many books that you can read.

image.describe: A library seen through a big window, with shelves full of books; Smarty the black cat reads a book with Lily.

items.note: Say 'cinema' for the place where people watch a film on a big screen.

image.describe: A cinema building with a big round popcorn icon and a film-reel icon above the door (no words); Smarty and Leo hold popcorn.

items.note: Say 'station' for the place where you get on a train.

image.describe: A train station with a long platform and a train arriving; Smarty the black cat waits with Omar, who holds a bag.

items.note: Say 'museum' for the place where people look at old and interesting things.

image.describe: A museum with tall columns and a big dinosaur skeleton visible in the hall; Smarty looks up at it with Zara.

practice.prompt: Where do you buy bread, milk and apples?
practice.explanation: A supermarket is a big shop for food.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for the place word after The.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.answer: I read a book in the library.
practice.explanation: You read books in a library.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: You buy apples at a supermarket, not at a library or museum.

practice.prompt: Where do people watch a film?
practice.explanation: A cinema has a big screen for films.

practice.prompt: Say the phrase aloud. You can retry if recognition mishears you.
practice.explanation: A station is for trains. You can also say The museum is big.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for the place word at the end.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: Is links the place with a describing word.

practice.prompt: Where do you take a train?
practice.explanation: You get on a train at a station.

story.hook: Smarty likes food. Which place does he like?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Look, Smarty! This is the library.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: I read a book in the library.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: I like the supermarket. I like food!

questions.explanation: Ana says she likes the cinema.
Ben says he likes the museum.
Ana says the station is big, too.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat, Ben and Ana lean on a balcony rail and look over a sunny town with a library, a cinema, a museum, a supermarket and a station.

mission.setup: You are on the balcony with Smarty. Tell him which place you like.

turns.smarty: I like the library. Do you like the library?
turns.hint: Answer Yes or No. You can also say which place you like.

turns.smarty: What do you like?
turns.hint: Say I like the + a place word.

lessons.title: Where is the bank?
lessons.scenario: Smarty has a town map. Ask where places are and say if they are near or far.

items.note: Say 'Where is' and the name of a place to ask how to find it.

items.example: The park is near the school.
items.note: Say 'near' when a place is close and you can get there quickly.
Say 'far' when a place is a long way away. It is the opposite of near.
A map is a picture of a town that shows where places are.

image.describe: A paper town map spread on a table with little pictures of a park, a bank and a school joined by roads; Smarty the black cat points at it with a paw.

practice.prompt: Ask about the bank.
practice.explanation: Where is + the + a place asks how to find it.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for the place after the.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.answer: The bank is near the park.
practice.explanation: Near says that two places are close.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.text: The hospital is not near. It is ___.
practice.explanation: Not near means far.

practice.prompt: You need money. Where do you go?
practice.explanation: A bank is the place for money.

practice.prompt: Say the phrase aloud. You can retry if recognition mishears you.
practice.explanation: This is how you ask where a place is.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for the last word. A map shows the town.

practice.prompt: Build the question.
practice.explanation: Where is the + a place always starts with Where.

practice.prompt: The station is far. Which word means not near?
practice.explanation: Far is the opposite of near.

story.hook: Is the station near? Smarty looks at the map.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: The bank is near the park.

questions.prompt: Which place does Smarty ask about first?
questions.explanation: Smarty first says Where is the bank?
Mia says the bank is near the park.

questions.prompt: Who says the station is far?
questions.explanation: Sam says the station is far.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat, Mia and Sam stand on a balcony around a small table with a town map; Mia points at a park on the map.

mission.setup: Smarty has a map of the town. Ask him where a place is, then tell him about your school.

turns.smarty: Hello! I have a map. What do you want?
turns.hint: Ask Where is the + a place word.

turns.smarty: Where is your school? Near or far?
turns.hint: Say near or far.

lessons.title: Turn left
lessons.scenario: Smarty is lost in the street. Tell him which way to go.

items.note: Say 'turn left' to tell someone to go to the left side.

image.describe: Seen from behind, Smarty the black cat stops at a crossing and turns to the left, with a big arrow icon pointing left.

items.note: Say 'turn right' to tell someone to go to the right side.

image.describe: Seen from behind, Smarty the black cat stops at a crossing and turns to the right, with a big arrow icon pointing right.

items.note: Say 'go straight on' when someone must not turn and must keep going the same way.

image.describe: A long straight road ahead; Smarty the black cat walks forward with a big arrow icon pointing straight up the road.

items.example: The café is on the corner.
items.note: The corner is the place where two streets meet.

image.describe: Two streets meet at the corner of a building; Smarty the black cat sits at the corner and a small café is on it.

practice.prompt: Which phrase tells Smarty to go to the left side?
practice.explanation: Left is one side and right is the other side.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for right and for the place word.

practice.prompt: Build the phrase.
practice.explanation: Go straight on means do not turn.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Turn left tells you to go to the left side.

practice.prompt: Ask where the bank is.
practice.explanation: Where is + the + a place asks how to find it.

practice.prompt: Say the phrase aloud. You can retry if recognition mishears you.
practice.explanation: You gave a short direction.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.answer: The café is on the corner.
practice.explanation: On the corner means where two streets meet.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.audio: Look at the map. Turn right.
practice.answer: Look at the map. Turn right.
options: Look at the map. Turn left.
Look at the map. Go straight on.
Look at the map. Turn right.
practice.explanation: Listen for the direction after the map.

practice.prompt: Which phrase is the opposite of Turn left?
practice.explanation: Left and right are opposites.

story.hook: Smarty is hungry. Which way is the café?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Yes. The café is on the corner.

questions.prompt: Where does Smarty want to go?
questions.explanation: Smarty asks Where is the café?
Ben says Turn left at the bank.
Ben says the café is on the corner.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat and Ben stand on a street corner; Ben points ahead and to the left, and a small café with tables is on the corner behind a bank.

mission.setup: Smarty is lost on a street. Give him directions.

turns.smarty: Where is the bank?
turns.hint: Say Turn left, Turn right or Go straight on.

turns.smarty: I am at the corner. Where is the park?
turns.hint: Give one direction. You can use the corner.

lessons.title: I can swim
lessons.canDo: Say what you can and can't do
lessons.scenario: Smarty and his friends talk about what they can do. Say what you can and cannot do.

items.note: Say 'I can' when you are able to do something.
Say 'I cannot' or 'I can't' for something you are not able to do.
To swim is to move in water.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat swims happily in a blue swimming pool while Mia watches from the side.

items.note: To ride a bike is to go along on two wheels.

image.describe: Sam rides a red bike along a park path while Smarty the black cat sits in the front basket.

practice.prompt: Say that you are able to swim.
practice.explanation: I can + an action word says you are able to do it.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for cannot. It means you are not able to.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: Can goes after I and before the action.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.text: I can swim, but I ___ ride a bike.
practice.explanation: But shows a different idea, so you use cannot.

practice.prompt: Mia asks: Can you swim? You can swim. What do you say?
practice.explanation: You answer a can-question with Yes, I can.

practice.prompt: You are able to read. Which sentence says it?
practice.explanation: I can + read says you are able to read.

practice.prompt: Say the phrase aloud. You can retry if recognition mishears you.
practice.explanation: You said what you are able to do.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: You can use can with many action words.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for can and for swim.

story.hook: Sam can swim. Can he ride a bike, too?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: No, I cannot ride a bike.

questions.explanation: Sam says Yes, I can swim.
Smarty says I can ride a bike.
Sam says I cannot ride a bike.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat, Mia and Sam on a balcony above a park; below them a child rides a bike and a pool is visible in the distance.

mission.setup: Smarty asks what you can do. Answer in your own words.

turns.smarty: I can ride a bike. Can you swim?
turns.hint: Answer Yes or No. You can say I can swim or I cannot swim.

turns.smarty: What can you do?
accept: ^i can (?:swim|ride a bike) and i can (?:read|cook)$
turns.hint: Say I can + an action. You can use swim, ride a bike, read or cook.

lessons.title: How do you go?
lessons.canDo: Say how you travel in town
lessons.scenario: Leo and Zara ask how you travel in town. Say how you go.

items.note: Say 'walk' when you go with your feet.

items.example: I go to school by bus.
items.note: Say 'by bus' when you travel in a bus.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat and Leo sit by a window on a bright green city bus.

items.example: I go to the park by car.
items.note: Say 'by car' when you travel in a car.

image.describe: A family car on a road with Ben driving and Smarty the black cat looking out of the back window.

items.example: I go to school on foot.
items.note: Say 'on foot' when you go with your feet. It means the same as walk.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat and Zara walk side by side on a sunny pavement, both taking a big step.

practice.prompt: Which phrase means you travel in a bus?
practice.explanation: By + bus says what you travel in.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.audio: I go to school by car.
practice.answer: I go to school by car.
options: I go to school by bus.
I go to school on foot.
I go to school by car.
practice.explanation: Listen for the last words.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: Walk and on foot both mean go with your feet.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: We say by bus and by car. We say on foot.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.answer: I walk to school every day.
practice.explanation: Every day shows what you do again and again.

practice.prompt: Say the phrase aloud. You can retry if recognition mishears you.
practice.text: I go to school by bus.
practice.answer: I go to school by bus.
practice.explanation: You said how you travel. Great!

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Usually means most days. Always means every day.

practice.prompt: You want to walk to the park. Which sentence is right?
practice.answer: I go to the park on foot.
options: I go to the park by bus.
I go to the park by car.
I go to the park on foot.
practice.explanation: On foot means with your feet.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for car.

story.hook: Zara and Leo go to the same school. Do they go the same way?

lines.speaker: Zara
lines.text: How do you go to school, Leo?

lines.speaker: Zara
lines.text: I walk. The school is near.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Smarty, look! There is a bus.

questions.prompt: How does Leo go to school?
questions.explanation: Leo says I go by bus.

questions.prompt: What does Zara say about the school?
questions.explanation: Zara says The school is near.
Leo says There is a bus.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat, Zara and Leo on a balcony above a street where a green bus stops at a school gate.

mission.setup: A new friend asks how you travel. Answer in your own words.

turns.smarty: How do you go to school?
turns.hint: Say I go by bus, by car or on foot. You can also say I walk.

turns.smarty: Is the school near or far?
turns.hint: Say near or far.

lessons.title: In the city
lessons.scenario: Ana and Omar show Smarty their town and a big city far away.

items.example: The bridge is on the road.
items.note: A bridge goes over a river so people can walk or drive across.

image.describe: A stone bridge over a wide blue river with a road across it; Smarty the black cat stands in the middle and looks at the water.

items.note: A road is the long way where cars, buses and bikes go.

image.describe: A long grey road with a white line in the middle going far between green fields; Smarty the black cat stands at the edge.

items.note: A city is a very big place with many buildings and many people.

image.describe: A big city skyline with tall buildings, roads and bridges seen from far away; Smarty the black cat sits on a hill and looks at it.

items.note: A town is a place with houses and shops. It is smaller than a city.

image.describe: A small town with low houses, a little square, a few shops and trees seen from above; Smarty the black cat sits on a roof.

practice.prompt: Which word is a very big place with tall buildings?
practice.explanation: A city is big. A town is smaller.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for town and for small.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.answer: The bridge is on the road.
practice.explanation: On the road says where the bridge is.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: You walk on a road. A city or a town is a big place.

practice.prompt: Ask where the bridge is.
practice.explanation: Where is + the + a word asks how to find it.

practice.prompt: Say the phrase aloud. You can retry if recognition mishears you.
practice.explanation: You described a city.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.audio: The road is near the school.
practice.answer: The road is near the school.
options: The road is far from the school.
The road is near the park.
The road is near the school.
practice.explanation: Listen for near and the last word.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.answer: The park is in the town.
practice.explanation: In the town says the park is inside the town.

practice.prompt: A city is big. Which one is small?
practice.explanation: A town is smaller than a city.

story.hook: Smarty looks at the town. Where is the big city?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Look, Smarty! This is my town.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: The town is small, but it is beautiful.

lines.speaker: Ana

turns.smarty: Do you live in a city or a town?

turns.smarty: Is it big or small?
turns.hint: Say big or small.

lessons.title: Opposite the park
lessons.scenario: Zara, Tom and Smarty talk about where places are in the town.

items.example: The café is opposite the park.
items.note: Say 'opposite' when two places face each other across a street.

items.example: The bank is between the school and the café.
items.note: Say 'between' for something in the middle of two other things.

items.example: The school is behind the bank.
items.note: Say 'behind' for something at the back of another thing.

items.example: The bus is in front of the school.
items.note: Say 'in front of' for something at the front of another thing.

practice.prompt: The café is across the road from the park. Say it.
practice.answer: The café is opposite the park.
options: The café is opposite the park.
The café is in front of the park.
The café is behind the park.
practice.explanation: Opposite means face to face across the road.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.audio: The bank is behind the school.
practice.answer: The bank is behind the school.
options: The bank is in front of the school.
The bank is next to the school.
The bank is behind the school.
practice.explanation: Listen for behind.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.answer: The library is between the bank and the school.
practice.explanation: Between needs two things: between A and B.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.text: The bus is in ___ of the school.

practice.prompt: Which sentence says the café is close beside the bank?

The café is opposite the bank.

practice.prompt: Say the phrase aloud. You can retry if recognition mishears you.
practice.text: The station is opposite the park.
practice.answer: The station is opposite the park.
practice.explanation: You said where a place is.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.audio: Where is the museum? It is behind the library.
practice.answer: Where is the museum? It is behind the library.
options: Where is the museum? It is opposite the library.
Where is the museum? It is near the library.
Where is the museum? It is behind the library.
practice.explanation: Listen for behind after the question.

practice.prompt: Match the opposites.
practice.explanation: Near and far are opposites; in front of and behind are opposites; left and right are opposites.

practice.prompt: The shop is in the middle of the bank and the café. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: Between means in the middle of two things.

lines.text: The bus is in front of the school!

questions.prompt: What is in front of the school?
questions.explanation: Smarty says the bus is in front of the school.

turns.smarty: And the café? Where is it?
accept: ^the caf[eé] is (?:near|opposite|behind|next to|in front of) the (?:park|school|hospital|bank|caf[eé]|supermarket|library|cinema|station|museum)$

lessons.title: Excuse me
lessons.scenario: Smarty is lost in the street. Ask a stranger politely for help.

items.example: Excuse me, where is the station?
items.note: Say 'Excuse me' to start talking to someone you do not know.
Ask 'Is it far?' to find out if a place is a long way away.

items.example: Turn left at the traffic lights.

image.describe: A street corner with a set of traffic lights showing red, yellow and green circles; Smarty the black cat waits at the crossing with Mia.

items.example: It is five minutes on foot.
items.note: We say minutes for a short time, like five minutes.

practice.prompt: You want to talk to someone you do not know. How do you start?

practice.answer: Excuse me, where is the library?
options: Excuse me, where is the station?
Excuse me, where is the bank?
Excuse me, where is the library?

practice.prompt: Build the question.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.

It is ten minutes by bus.

practice.prompt: Ask a stranger politely where the station is.

lessons.title: A walk with Smarty
lessons.scenario: Smarty wants to see the town. Help him get to a place with a ticket and a bus.

items.note: A taxi is a car with a driver that you pay to take you to a place.

image.describe: A yellow taxi with a lit sign on its roof stops at the kerb; Smarty the black cat looks out of the window.

items.note: A ticket is a small paper that lets you travel on a bus or a train.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat holds up two small paper tickets with a star on them and smiles.

items.note: Say 'Let's go' when you want to start and go together.

items.example: The bus stop is near the school.
items.note: A bus stop is the place where you wait for a bus.

image.describe: A bus stop with a shelter, a bench and a pole with a bus icon; Smarty the black cat and Ben wait there.

practice.prompt: It is a car with a driver. You pay to go. Which word is it?
practice.explanation: A taxi is a car you pay to ride in.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for ticket.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: Let's go means we go together.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.text: I buy a ___ at the station.
practice.explanation: You buy a ticket at the station.

practice.prompt: Ask the price of a ticket.
practice.explanation: How much is it? asks the price.

practice.prompt: Say the phrase aloud. You can retry if recognition mishears you.
practice.text: Let's go to the bus stop.
practice.answer: Let's go to the bus stop.
practice.explanation: You said we go together.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.audio: Excuse me, where is the bus stop?
practice.answer: Excuse me, where is the bus stop?
options: Excuse me, where is the station?
Excuse me, where is the park?
Excuse me, where is the bus stop?
practice.explanation: Listen for bus stop at the end.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: By taxi says what you travel in.

practice.prompt: You want to walk. Which phrase says that?
practice.explanation: On foot means with your feet.

story.hook: Ben and Smarty want to go to the museum. How do they go?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Let's go to the museum, Smarty!

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: No, it is ten minutes by bus.

questions.prompt: Where do Ben and Smarty go?
questions.explanation: Ben says Let's go to the museum.
Ben says it is ten minutes by bus.
Ben says it is near the bank.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat and Ben walk to a bus stop near a bank; Ben holds up two tickets and a bus is arriving.

mission.setup: Smarty wants to go to the park. Help him get there.

turns.smarty: Let's go to the park! How do we go?
turns.hint: Say by bus, by taxi, by car or on foot.

turns.smarty: Where is the bus stop?
turns.hint: Say where it is or give a direction.

turns.smarty: I have a ticket. Look!
turns.hint: Say Let's go!
